baseline.name: Literal queue-rotation simulation
baseline.approach: Rotate students who reject the next sandwich, stopping after a complete unsuccessful round.
baseline.time: O(n*m) conservative worst-case rotations for n students and m sandwiches

why: Only availability of each binary preference matters: rotations cannot help once no remaining student wants the next sandwich.
quantitative_comparison: The archive counts n students once and inspects at most m sandwiches, avoiding repeated queue rotations and queue storage. This is an operation-growth comparison, not a measured time ratio.
tradeoffs: Depends on the binary preference domain and the problem's freely rotating queue rules. Other scheduling constraints would invalidate the aggregate-count model.
evidence_basis: Static queue/count equivalence under the stated problem rules; no empirical benchmark.
